input.quote: The Issuer is relying on each applicable Originator's or the Servicer's Eligibility Representation in acquiring the Receivables, which Eligibility Representation will survive the transfer and absolute assignment of the Receivables by the Depositor to the Issuer under this Agreement and the pledge of the Receivables to the Indenture Trustee under the Indenture.
input.rationale: Translated to this receivables-transfer/servicing structure, the warranty package exceeds the preferred position and no redline is warranted. (1) Performance standard: Section 3.2(a) (p0082) requires the Servicer to "manage, service, administer and collect on the Receivables with reasonable care using that degree of skill and attention that the Servicer exercises for all comparable device payment plan agreement receivables that it services for itself or others according to the Servicing Procedures" — the industry-standard/workmanlike-manner analogue. (2) Conformance warranty: the Originators' and Servicer's Eligibility Representation about each Receivable (Section 2.5(a), p0071) is not period-limited at all; it expressly survives the transfer and the Indenture pledge (and the Section 2.4(b) security-interest reps survive termination and may not be waived), which is materially longer than the preferred 12 months. (3) Real remedy: Sections 2.5(b)/(c) and 2.6 give a mandatory reacquisition/acquisition obligation at the Acquisition Amount for uncured breaches with a material adverse effect — economically the "refund" limb of repair/replace/refund — backed by Section 3.3 acquisition obligations for the Servicer's own breaches and, importantly, the Section 11.2 dispute-resolution backstop (p0450) allowing the Issuer, Indenture Trustee or Noteholders to compel mediation or binding arbitration if a repurchase request is unresolved after 180 days. (4) Compliance with laws is separately warranted at Section 6.1(a)(ix) (p0268) plus Servicing Procedures compliance at 6.1(a)(x). No "AS IS" language or implied-warranty disclaimer exists anywhere in the agreement, so nothing swallows the express representations. Noted but not flagged: the "sole remedy" framing in Sections 2.5(c)/2.6(b)/3.3(g) and the willful-misconduct/bad-faith/gross-negligence liability standard in Section 6.2(a) narrow recourse, but these are standard ABS constructs and the mandatory repurchase remains a specific, enforceable obligation; the malicious-code limb of the preferred position has no application to a receivables pool.
